digest.headline: United States consumer prices rose above expectations in August as annual inflation held at 3.4 percent.

lede.b: The annual rate of inflation, which is the speed at which prices for everyday goods and services increase, held steady at 3.4% in the United States in August. This happened because the core consumer price index, a measure of price changes for a basket of goods, came in higher than analysts expected. Fuel costs accelerated sharply, pushing diesel prices past $6 per gallon due to conflict in the Middle East. Stock futures, which are contracts to buy shares at a set price in the future, still climbed because a recent rally in oil prices cooled down. The United States dollar also edged higher against the euro in response to the price data.
lede.i: United States inflation held at 3.4% in August as the core consumer price index increased beyond expectations. Accelerating fuel costs, driven by diesel prices surpassing $6 per gallon amid Middle East conflict, supported the print. Stock futures subsequently climbed by triple digits as a recent oil rally cooled, relieving broader equity pressures. The US dollar edged higher against the euro in response to the data release.
lede.a: US core inflation printed above consensus in August, anchoring annual headline prints at 3.4% on the back of diesel vector acceleration past $6 per gallon. Equity index futures decoupled positively from the energy impulse, staging a triple-digit relief rally as the preceding crude momentum mean-reverted. The US dollar responded via immediate spot appreciation against the euro along the front-end rate transmission channel.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: Stock futures rise and inflation data releases in August

stories.t: Stock Futures Rise as Oil Rally Cools
stories.b: Stock futures for the Dow and Nasdaq indexes rose by triple digits. Stock indexes track groups of company shares, which are small slices of ownership in a business. This increase happened as the recent rapid rise in oil prices slowed down. Lower oil price growth often helps calm market nerves.
stories.i: Dow and Nasdaq futures climbed by triple digits. The upward move followed a cooling in the recent oil rally. Lower energy costs relieved pressure on broader equity markets.
stories.a: Dow and Nasdaq futures advanced by triple digits as the underlying oil rally lost momentum. The compression in crude prices alleviated near-term margin pressures across major equity sectors. Market participants recalibrated positioning following the reversal in energy input costs.

stories.t: August Consumer Prices Rise Above Expectations
stories.b: The core consumer price index, a measure of how much everyday goods and services cost, rose more than expected in August. Prices stayed at a rate of 3.4% for the month. Higher fuel costs, including diesel passing $6 a gallon, pushed prices up due to conflict in the Middle East. The US dollar went up against the euro after this news.
stories.i: The US core consumer price index increased more than expected in August. Annual inflation held at 3.4% as fuel costs accelerated, with diesel prices surpassing $6 per gallon due to Middle East conflict. The US dollar edged higher against the euro in response to the data.
stories.a: The core consumer price index printed above consensus expectations for August. Headline inflation printed at 3.4% amid surging diesel prices exceeding $6 per gallon, driven by Middle East geopolitical conflict. The greenback extended gains against the euro as rates traders adjusted duration bets.

politics.b: Government reports showed inflation holding at 3.4% in August. Higher fuel prices linked to Middle East conflict drove the numbers.
politics.i: Official data confirmed annual inflation remained at 3.4% in August. Geopolitical conflict in the Middle East drove energy costs higher.
politics.a: Macroeconomic releases placed headline inflation at 3.4% for August. Middle East conflict transmission channels operated primarily through energy commodity spikes.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: UK economy grows, inflation expectations drop, and rate holds

stories.t: UK Economic Growth and AI Spending in July
stories.b: The UK economy grew in July. A large spending surge on artificial intelligence helped drive this growth forward. People and companies spent heavily on new technology tools. This boosted economic output for the month.
stories.i: The UK economy expanded in July. An artificial intelligence spending splurge provided the main growth impetus. Output rose across the technology sector as commercial deployment accelerated.
stories.a: UK economic output registered growth in July, underpinned by an artificial intelligence capital expenditure surge. This commercial tech deployment offset softer metrics elsewhere in the domestic output data. The data print keeps growth tracking above trend for the third quarter.

stories.t: Bank of England Public Expectations and Rate Outlook
stories.b: The Bank of England is the country's central bank, which sets borrowing costs. It reported a sharp drop in public inflation expectations. This drop followed a change in the survey provider used to ask people questions. Meanwhile, Bank of America expects the central bank to hold its key interest rate steady at the September meeting.
stories.i: The Bank of England reported a sharp drop in public inflation expectations following a survey provider change. Bank of America expects the central bank to hold its key rate in September. Analysts at the bank also flagged rising risks of future rate hikes.
stories.a: The Bank of England registered a sharp contraction in public inflation expectations following a methodological shift in survey provision. Bank of America models a hold at the upcoming September policy meeting while flagging asymmetric risks of subsequent rate hikes from sticky wage pressures.

politics.b: Jim O'Neill discussed the state of the UK economy and taxation policy in a media interview. Observers noted his comments on public finances. Politicians continue to debate tax rules.
politics.i: Jim O'Neill discussed UK economic performance and taxation frameworks during a Bloomberg appearance. The commentary addressed fiscal pressures facing public administration. Policy debates remain focused on revenue generation.
politics.a: Jim O'Neill evaluated UK macroeconomic trajectories and fiscal levers on Bloomberg. The discussion dissected structural tax burdens and growth constraints. Debates center on fiscal headroom limits.

timeline: Bank of America forecasts a key interest rate hold by the Bank of England in September.

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: DAX rebounds, Bundesbank warns on rates

stories.t: Frankfurt Index Recovers
stories.b: The DAX index in Frankfurt opened 0.40% higher on Friday. Shares in Deutsche Börse gained ground after previously lagging behind other stocks. Investors also looked closely at recent growth figures and awaited a US price report.
stories.i: The DAX index rose 0.40% at the open on Friday. Deutsche Börse shares advanced after acting as a recent laggard in the index. Traders monitored domestic growth data ahead of a US inflation release.
stories.a: The DAX opened up 0.40% on Friday, led by outperformance in Deutsche Börse following a period as a relative index laggard. Positioning adjusted ahead of the US CPI print, with market participants weighing localized growth prints against broader rate trajectory implications.

stories.t: Bundesbank Chief Warns on Further Tightening
stories.b: Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel stated that more borrowing cost increases depend heavily on energy costs. He warned that the European Central Bank may need to enter mildly restrictive territory even if it slows economic growth. European stocks faced their worst week since April following a recent rate increase.
stories.i: Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel stated that future rate increases remain dependent on energy costs. He warned that the central bank might need to enter mildly restrictive territory despite the drag on growth. European equities headed for their worst week since April following the recent central bank tightening.
stories.a: Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel conditioned subsequent rate hikes on energy cost trajectories while signalling a potential necessity to push policy into mildly restrictive territory. The rhetoric accompanied a broader equity drawdown, leaving European indices on track for their worst weekly performance since April in the wake of the latest central bank hike.

politics.b: Central bank leaders discussed how interest rates affect the wider economy and energy prices. Politicians watched the ongoing debate about economic growth versus tighter monetary policy. Officials balanced price stability goals against factory output concerns.
politics.i: Monetary authorities weighed restrictive policy against slowing growth metrics. Central bank officials tied future rate decisions directly to volatile energy price inputs. Lawmakers observed the tension between cooling price pressures and industrial stagnation.
politics.a: Governing council members debated the threshold for mildly restrictive policy settings amid softening regional macroeconomic indicators. Central bank communication explicitly conditioned subsequent normalization steps on external energy supply shocks. Policymakers navigated the trade-off between anchoring long-term expectations and compounding industrial deceleration.

timeline: Bundesbank President Nagel links further rate increases to energy costs.
DAX opens 0.40% higher in Frankfurt ahead of US data.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Yen moves and Bank of Japan tightening expectations

stories.t: Japanese Yen Shifts Against the US Dollar
stories.b: The Japanese yen, which is the money used in Japan, went up in value compared to the US dollar. The US dollar lost some of its upward push after new inflation data came out. Inflation is the speed at which prices go up over time. Later in the London trading session, the yen dropped back down into the low 154 range against the dollar. Traders are also keeping an eye on oil prices reaching triple digits.
stories.i: The Japanese yen rallied as the US dollar lost momentum following recent inflation readings. Market participants later pushed the yen down into the low 154 range during London trading hours. Meanwhile, rising oil prices and shifting yield differentials continue to drive currency volatility. Further currency appreciation risks constraining the central bank's policy path.
stories.a: The Japanese yen appreciated as post-inflation US dollar momentum stalled, though spot subsequently retraced to the low 154 handle in London. Yield pressure against US Treasuries creates structural headwinds for the currency, complicating the central bank's tightening calculus. Rapid appreciation risks constraining policy normalization by tightening financial conditions prematurely.

stories.t: Bank of Japan Tightening Outlook and Corporate Debt
stories.b: Market bets on an extended tightening cycle by the Bank of Japan grew stronger this week. Tightening means a central bank is raising interest rates to slow down the economy and control prices. DBS analysts noted that prospects for a hawkish rate hike are increasing. Hawkish means favoring higher interest rates. Meanwhile, HSBC issued three series of yen-denominated callable bonds.
stories.i: Market participants increased bets on an extended tightening cycle by the Bank of Japan this week. Analysts at DBS highlighted growing prospects for a hawkish rate hike. Yield pressures continue to influence currency valuations against the US dollar according to OCBC commentary. Concurrently, HSBC issued three series of yen-denominated callable bonds.
stories.a: Market pricing reflects an extended tightening cycle from the Bank of Japan, with DBS noting rising prospects for a hawkish rate hike. Yield differentials remain a primary transmission channel for currency weakness against the greenback as highlighted by OCBC. Meanwhile, corporate primary issuance active in the debt capital markets included three series of yen-denominated callable bonds by HSBC.

politics.b: China raised visa fees for Japanese citizens on a reciprocal basis. Tokyo markets dealt with varying currency rates and global financial news. Financial reports also noted higher oil prices.
politics.i: China implemented reciprocal visa fee increases for Japanese citizens. Tokyo markets absorbed currency fluctuations alongside broader macroeconomic data releases. Oil prices continued to trade at elevated levels.
politics.a: Chinese authorities raised visa fees for Japanese citizens on a reciprocal basis. Tokyo markets processed these diplomatic friction points alongside triple-digit oil benchmarks and ongoing foreign exchange volatility.

China.label: China
China.sub: Enflame surges on debut as tech and industrial firms report

stories.t: Enflame Shares Surge in Shanghai Debut
stories.b: Shares in a company called Enflame nearly tripled on its first day of trading in Shanghai. The firm makes artificial intelligence chips, which are computer parts that power smart software. Tencent backs the business, meaning the giant technology company invested money in it. The stock market price jumped by 179% as buyers bet on high demand for these specialized chips.
stories.i: Enflame shares surged by 179% during its Shanghai Stock Exchange debut. The artificial intelligence chip designer is backed by Tencent. Investors bid up the stock amid strong demand for advanced computing hardware.
stories.a: Enflame shares nearly tripled in its Shanghai listing, closing up 179% on robust artificial intelligence hardware demand. The Tencent-backed chip maker capitalized on heavy domestic allocations toward domestic semiconductor alternatives.

stories.t: Geely Launches Galaxy TT Starting at 129,900 Yuan
stories.b: Geely launched a new vehicle named the Galaxy TT at a price of 129,900 yuan, or $19,100. This price is half of what a Tesla costs. The car uses an 800-volt platform, which is an electrical system that helps the battery charge quickly.
stories.i: Geely released the Galaxy TT starting at 129,900 yuan, or $19,100. The electric vehicle costs half the price of a Tesla model. The vehicle operates on an 800-volt electrical architecture.
stories.a: Geely priced the Galaxy TT at 129,900 yuan, undercutting Tesla by half at a $19,100 equivalent entry point. The platform utilizes an 800-volt electrical architecture for fast charging capabilities.

stories.t: Kaifa Technology Plans Advanced Packaging Investment
stories.b: Kaifa Technology will spend 1.85 billion yuan on an advanced packaging expansion. The project targets a production level of 10,000 wafers per month using a 2.5D manufacturing method.
stories.i: Kaifa Technology allocated 1.85 billion yuan toward an advanced packaging expansion. The facility targets a capacity of 10,000 wafers per month for 2.5D packaging.
stories.a: Kaifa Technology deployed 1.85 billion yuan into advanced packaging expansion. The capital expenditure targets a throughput of 10,000 wafers per month for 2.5D semiconductor integration.

politics.b: The Chinese government set plans to expand how much the yuan is used around the world between 2026 and 2030. At the same time, authorities raised prices for gasoline and diesel fuel. China also raised visa fees for visitors from Japan.
politics.i: The State Council Information Office outlined plans to expand the global use of the yuan from 2026 to 2030. Regulators raised domestic gasoline and diesel prices. Meanwhile, China increased visa fees for Japanese citizens on a reciprocal basis.
politics.a: The State Council Information Office published guidelines to expand international yuan adoption through 2030. Pricing authorities adjusted domestic gasoline and diesel prices upward. Reciprocal visa fee increases were implemented for Japanese nationals.

timeline: Enflame shares nearly triple in Shanghai debut

India.label: India
India.sub: RBI liquidity operations, government bond auctions, and currency pressures

stories.t: Reserve Bank of India Absorbs Liquidity Through Reverse Repo Auctions
stories.b: The central bank of India manages how much money circulates in the financial system. It held two separate variable rate reverse repo auctions on September 11, 2026. These events let banks store extra cash with the central bank for a set period. Financial institutions offered 3,44,800 crore rupees for a 4-day tenor and 60,449 crore rupees for a 26-day tenor. Both auctions yielded a cut-off rate of 5.24 percent.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India absorbed excess banking system liquidity using short-term and medium-term liquidity adjustment facility tools. It allotted 3,44,864 crore rupees in a 4-day variable rate reverse repo auction at a cut-off rate of 5.24 percent. A separate 26-day tenor auction accepted 60,449 crore rupees at the identical rate of 5.24 percent.
stories.a: The central bank sterilized surplus liquidity via dual-tenor variable rate reverse repo operations under the liquidity adjustment facility. Bidding patterns showed 3,44,864 crore rupees accepted across the 4-day window against a 5,00,000 crore rupee notified amount, alongside 60,449 crore rupees taken for the 26-day tenor. Both auctions cleared at a uniform weighted average rate of 5.24 percent.

stories.t: Government Debt Sells at Recent Auctions While Rupee Declines
stories.src: Reserve Bank of India · India markets
stories.b: The Indian government sold debt to investors on September 11, 2026, including 6.20% GS 2029 securities and a new 2056 bond. Meanwhile, the Indian rupee suffered its largest weekly drop in four months. Higher crude oil costs and rising bond yields drove the currency lower for the fourth consecutive day. Stock indexes also reacted as the Nifty Metal index fell 3 percent due to regional tensions in West Asia.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India published auction results for government stock maturing in 2029, 2033, and 2056, accepting 4,505.529 crore rupees for the partial 2029 tranche. Simultaneously, the Indian rupee posted its sharpest weekly decline in four months. Rising crude oil prices and increasing yields pressured the currency across four consecutive sessions.
stories.a: The debt management office issued paper across the 2029, 2033, and 2056 tenors, accepting 4,505.529 crore rupees for the partial 6.20% 2029 GS issue at an implicit yield of 6.4031 percent. Concurrently, macroeconomic headwinds drove the rupee to its steepest weekly contraction in four months. Crude oil appreciation and upward yield trajectories spurred foreign exchange outflows over four consecutive trading sessions.

politics.b: The central bank extended administrative directions for The Gujarat Rajya Karmachari Co-op. Bank Ltd until September 11, 2026.
politics.i: The Reserve Bank of India extended regulatory directions under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, for The Gujarat Rajya Karmachari Co-op. Bank Ltd until September 11, 2026.
politics.a: Regulatory oversight persisted for The Gujarat Rajya Karmachari Co-op. Bank Ltd via an extension of directions under Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, running until the close of business on September 11, 2026.

timeline: The Reserve Bank of India issued directions to The Gujarat Rajya Karmachari Co-op. Bank Ltd.
The Reserve Bank of India conducted variable rate reverse repo auctions and government stock sales.

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Petrobras plans fuel price adjustments and secures deals

stories.t: Petrobras Weighs Fuel Price Adjustments
stories.b: Petrobras wants to raise diesel prices. It is waiting for government steps to protect consumers first. Meanwhile, the company cancelled a gasoline hike. The gasoline price fell by R$0.19 following tax cuts.
stories.i: Petrobras seeks to implement a diesel price increase while awaiting government measures to protect consumers. The company simultaneously cancelled a planned gasoline hike, leaving the price down by R$0.19 after tax cuts.
stories.a: Petrobras targets a diesel price adjustment conditional on fiscal or regulatory shielding mechanisms from the state. Management cancelled the separate gasoline hike, allowing prices to decline by R$0.19 following structural tax reductions.

stories.t: Braskem Extends Supply Deal With Petrobras
stories.b: Braskem extended its natural gas supply agreement with Petrobras. The deal runs through 2029. Petrobras also drew $1.4bn in bids for a subsea tender.
stories.i: Braskem prolonged its natural gas supply agreement with Petrobras through 2029. Petrobras separately secured $1.4bn in bids for a subsea tender.
stories.a: Braskem extended its natural gas procurement contract with Petrobras through 2029, locking in feedstock visibility. Petrobras concurrently drew $1.4bn in bids for its subsea tender, reflecting robust offshore capital expenditure pipelines.

politics.b: The government is looking at steps to protect consumers from diesel price changes. Petrobras has to wait for these official measures.
politics.i: State involvement shapes fuel pricing as Petrobras awaits government measures to shield consumers before raising diesel costs.
politics.a: State intervention constrains pricing autonomy as Petrobras conditions its diesel tariff hike on explicit government consumer-shielding policies.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: Oil output drops and corporate deals emerge in Saudi Arabia

stories.t: Saudi Petroleum Output Hits Multi-Decade Low
stories.b: Saudi Arabia produces crude oil, which is the raw liquid pumped from the ground and turned into petrol. The International Energy Agency says that Saudi oil supply fell to a level not seen in more than thirty years. This drop happened following Houthi attacks and fallout from the war between the United States and Iran.
stories.i: Saudi crude output fell to its lowest level in more than three decades according to the International Energy Agency. The drop followed Houthi attacks and the wider fallout from the conflict between the United States and Iran.
stories.a: Saudi oil supply contracted to a more than three-decade low per International Energy Agency data following Houthi kinetic strikes and regional spillovers from the US-Iran conflict.

stories.t: Aramco Considers Arlanxeo Divestment and Pricing Shift
stories.b: Asian buyers asked Saudi Aramco to change how it prices crude oil to use the Brent benchmark. At the same time, reports show that Saudi Aramco is considering selling Arlanxeo. Aramco Ventures also backed a funding round for a company named DeepCtrls.
stories.i: Asian buyers asked Saudi Aramco to switch its crude pricing mechanism to Brent. Simultaneously, Saudi Aramco is weighing a sale of Arlanxeo according to reports. Aramco Ventures also participated in a funding round for DeepCtrls alongside lead investor CATL.
stories.a: Asian clients requested that Saudi Aramco re-benchmark its crude pricing to Brent. Parallel reports indicate that Saudi Aramco is evaluating strategic options for Arlanxeo, while Aramco Ventures co-funded a physical AI round for DeepCtrls led by CATL.

politics.b: The Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia is reportedly thinking about a merger between Electronic Arts and Savvy Games Group.
politics.i: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund is reportedly considering a merger of Electronic Arts and Savvy Games Group.
politics.a: The Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia is evaluating a potential consolidation involving Electronic Arts and Savvy Games Group.

timeline: The International Energy Agency reported that Saudi oil supply fell to a multi-decade low.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Naira rises against major currencies and oil production climbs

stories.t: Naira climbs against dollar and euro
stories.b: The Nigerian naira is the official money used in Nigeria. It grew stronger against the United States dollar and the euro. The Central Bank of Nigeria sold $151m to help the currency market. Foreign currency reserves also reached $54bn, which is an 18-year high.
stories.i: The naira appreciated to N1,328.22 per dollar on September 11, 2026. This recovery followed $151m in sales by the central bank. Meanwhile, external reserves climbed to an 18-year high of $54bn, pushing the naira to N1,548 per euro.
stories.a: Intervention by the Central Bank of Nigeria via $151m in liquidity injection catalyzed the naira's appreciation to N1,328.22 against the dollar. Concurrently, external reserves scaling to an 18-year high of $54bn provided broad support, driving the exchange rate to N1,548 per euro.

stories.t: Nigeria crude oil output increases
stories.b: Oil production is a huge part of Nigeria's economy. Output reached 1,573,000 barrels per day. This increase happened alongside an overall rise in production across OPEC countries.
stories.i: Nigeria lifted its oil production to 1,573,000 barrels per day. This output expansion coincided with broader production gains across the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries.
stories.a: Crude output scaled to 1,573,000 barrels per day as broader OPEC production aggregates shifted upward. This volume expansion directly affects federal revenue generation and foreign exchange earnings.

politics.b: The government faces a major housing crisis. The cost of building materials has gone up drastically across the country.
politics.i: Soaring construction material costs generated a severe housing crisis across the country.
politics.a: Escalating construction material prices precipitated a nationwide housing crisis.

timeline: Nigeria oil output reaches 1,573,000 barrels per day.
External reserves hit an 18-year high of $54bn.

Australia.label: Australia
Australia.sub: Australian economic growth slows as multiple equities near ex-dividend dates

stories.t: Australian Gross Domestic Product Expands by 0.4 Percent
stories.b: The Australian economy grew by 0.4% recently. This number shows how much the total value of goods and services produced in the country went up. People are now asking if high interest rates, which are like the cost of borrowing money that stays expensive for a long time, are starting to slow down business activity. The recent growth figure of 0.4% is the data point released for the period.
stories.i: The Australian economy expanded by 0.4%. Analysts question whether the persistent high-interest-rate environment is beginning to weigh on domestic activity. This modest expansion rate marks the latest reading on national output.
stories.a: Real GDP growth printed at 0.4%, intensifying debate over whether the restrictive monetary policy stance is biting into economic momentum. The sequential print underscores the tension between persistent policy tightness and domestic resilience.

stories.t: Focus Minerals Posts 29.4 Percent Margin While Other ASX Equities Approach Ex-Dividend Deadlines
stories.b: Focus Minerals shares look cheap because the company has a 29.4% margin, which is the money left over after paying costs. At the same time, companies like WCM Global Growth and Glennon Small Companies are nearing their ex-dividend dates, which are the cut-off times to qualify for a company's cash payout to shareholders. Other firms reaching this point include Saunders International, Kelsian Group, Ramelius Resources, and Virgin Australia Holdings. Reece Group shares went up over 56% in a year. VEEM Limited shares dropped nearly 60% over the same period. Perenti fell nearly 13%, and Nuix dropped 23%.
stories.i: Focus Minerals shares trade with support from a 29.4% profit margin. Multiple companies, including WCM Global Growth, Glennon Small Companies, Saunders International, Kelsian Group, Ramelius Resources, and Virgin Australia Holdings, approach their ex-dividend dates. Over a one-year timeframe, Reece Group shares gained over 56%, VEEM Limited declined nearly 60%, Perenti dropped nearly 13%, and Nuix fell 23%.
stories.a: Focus Minerals equity valuation draws support from an underlying 29.4% margin. Concurrently, market participants monitor the ex-dividend approach for WCM Global Growth, Glennon Small Companies, Saunders International, Kelsian Group, Ramelius Resources, and Virgin Australia Holdings. Over the trailing twelve-month period, Reece Group appreciated over 56%, VEEM Limited contracted by nearly 60%, Perenti receded by almost 13%, and Nuix dropped 23%.

politics.b: Australian market reports noted economic growth figures of 0.4%. Various company share updates were published on the ASX. No specific government policy decisions or political votes were detailed in the updates.
politics.i: Market reports detailed an economic growth print of 0.4% alongside corporate updates across multiple ASX equities. The coverage contained no references to legislative votes or executive policy announcements.
politics.a: Data releases centered on the 0.4% GDP expansion and corporate equity valuations across the ASX universe. The source reporting omitted any engagement with fiscal policy parameters or legislative proceedings.

timeline: Focus Minerals highlights a 29.4% margin while Australian economic growth prints at 0.4%
